data.name: Bindhavi
data.gender_notes: Bindhavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess Bindu, the embodiment of devotion, represents the supreme soul, the ultimate reality. She is the source of all love and compassion. The name Bindhavi carries the meaning “Goddess of Devotion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bindhavi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of devotion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the divine essence of devotion and love.
data.etymology: Bindhavi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Devotion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bindhavi total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bindhavi" is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bindu', which signifies a bind or tie. This name was popular among the Hindu communities due to its profound religious connection with the goddess Bindu. Goddess Bindu represents the focus point or focalization of consciousness, leading individuals towards spiritual growth and inner transformation. Hindus use this name for their daughters, believing it will instill love, compassion, and inner strength.
data.spiritual_significance: Goddess Bindu signifies the embodiment of pure devotion. She is the supreme source of all love, compassion, and grace. In Hinduism, the syllable 'Bindu' is the symbol for spiritual focus and awakening. It represents the ultimate reality and the unmanifested universe. By invoking Goddess Bindu, individuals seek to connect with their inner selves and the divine presence within. Through her blessings, they attain peace, serenity, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Bindhavi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bindu', meaning drop or point of consciousness. It symbolizes the deep inner connection between the individual soul and the divine. The name evokes a sense of devotion and surrender towards the higher self.

historical_references.reference: Bindhavi, also known as Bindusara or Vipula, was a king of the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan plateau of India during the 4th century CE. He is known for his patronage of art and architecture, particularly in the Buddhist and Jain traditions.

historical_references.reference: Bindhavi is also the name of a famous Hindu temple located in Karnataka, India. The temple is believed to have been built during the Hoysala Empire in the 12th or 13th century CE and is known for its intricate sculptures and architectural design.
